status: Frozen after source inspection, before baseline tests and native case execution
question: Does pinned RAC rollback distinguish an explicitly failed compensation result from a completed compensation, and what fixture state remains?
population: Eight source-informed authored conditions, one fresh inert SQLite fixture each: core success; core explicit error result; core raised exception; native adapter success; native adapter raised-before-change; native adapter partial-change-then-raise; native adapter missing compensation tool; native adapter success-returning no-op.
baseline: Run the unchanged acquired tests/core/test_recovery_manager.py and record every pass/failure. Do not relabel a baseline failure as a finding or silently repair upstream tests.
execution: Use unchanged core modules, the exact pinned LangChainToolExecutor adapter loaded directly from its file, authored invoke-compatible local tool objects and an explicit passthrough parameter extractor. This is not a full LangChain agent/model experiment. Disable dynamic matching and LLM tool alternatives; no network or real credentials.
world: SQLite tables contain one synthetic session-active flag and one synthetic artifact row. Forward creation commits both. A successful compensator revokes the fixture session and deletes the artifact. An independent read-only SQLite connection observes both endpoints before and after rollback. These flags are fixture state, not real credential revocation or compromise-removal efficacy.
measurements: Forward output and statuses, executor result and explicit-status detector classification, rollback return or exception, record status, compensated/failed identities, number of actual tool invocations, session flag and artifact count. Keep record identities separate from resource identifiers.
controls: Success must establish the fixture's expected cleaned state. An exception exposed directly to the core is a failure-path control. A success-returning no-op tests the limit of trusting returned success: residual state in that condition alone is not evidence that the library can infer hidden external effects.
analysis: Report all eight conditions, not a statistical failure rate. An explicit error returned by the native adapter followed by compensated bookkeeping is an artifact-specific result-handling mismatch candidate. State restoration, output-status interpretation and whole workflow recovery remain separate endpoints.
limits: Source-informed, deterministic local fixtures; no blind sampling, natural workflows, model calls, process crash, concurrent writers, fresh OS, field-wide novelty or deployment exploit. The existing effect-anomaly literature already studies missing/duplicated effects and compensation limits. No preprint is justified solely by selecting an acknowledged limitation.
